_about: Walkback mission policy. Every limit the planner enforces lives here with its source. 'basis' is 'sourced' (a published number), 'derived' (computed from sourced numbers) or 'assumed' (our placeholder; a mission would set it). Edit this file to apply your own rules; the app reloads it on start.

max_slope_deg.source: NASA xEVA System Concept of Operations, EVA-EXP-0042 Rev B (2020), p.38: walking up/down/across slopes up to 20 deg (Apollo 15 ~17 deg).

caution_slope_deg.source: Walkback caution band below the 20 deg limit.

pace_kmh.source: EVA-EXP-0042 Rev B p.40: traverses assume ~2 km/hr walking pace over relatively level regolith (lunar).

eva_planned_h.source: EVA-EXP-0042 Rev B p.89: planned EVA excursions 4-8 h (6 +/- 2 h). We use the 6 h centre.

consumables_h.source: Walk-back criterion capacity: elapsed time + walk-back time must stay under this at every point. 8 h = upper end of the 4-8 h range in EVA-EXP-0042 p.89; a real suit's consumables and reserve would replace it.

consumables_reserve_min.source: Reserve kept back from the consumables capacity.

station_min.source: Default time on station per science stop.

egress_ingress_min.source: Airlock egress + ingress overhead inside the planned EVA time.

sunset_margin_min.source: Be back inside this long before sunset (from MEDA sunset climatology).

cold_limit_c.source: Caution if forecast air temperature (MEDA climatology, 1.45 m) drops below this during the EVA.

effort_ref_w.source: Average walking-effort reference (= 1600 BTU/h). Carried over from the prototype; source not verified. Effort is an index, not a flight value.

suit_mass_kg.source: Suit + carried load. Only used in the 'high' effort case.

shelter_quiet_min.source: Quiet space weather: no extra radiation limit; the consumables walk-back criterion binds. Baseline GCR dose still reported (RAD ~0.64 mSv/day).

shelter_watch_min.source: Watch (Mars-directed CME predicted in 24-72 h): our placeholder. There is no agreed definition of time-to-shelter for Mars (Loewe et al. 2025, arXiv:2502.02469).

shelter_warning_min.source: Warning: stay within 30 min of shelter. A RAD-based nowcast can give >= 30 min to avoid the SEP peak and most of the dose (Loewe et al. 2025, arXiv:2502.02469; ~50 min for the 20 May 2024 event).

warning_blocks_new_eva.source: No new EVA starts under a Warning; the plan is shown as NO-GO with a reduced alternative.

watch_hours.source: CME arrival predicted within this window -> Watch.

warning_hours.source: CME arrival predicted within this window (or arrived in the past 12 h) -> Warning.

warning_past_hours.source: Keep Warning this long after a predicted arrival.

buddy_assist_pace_factor.source: Pace when one crew member helps an impaired partner (buddy rule contingency). Used for the 'assisted walk-back' ETA.

hazard_route_weight.source: Route cost multiplier = 1 + weight x terrain hazard (0..1).

hazard_caution.source: Terrain hazard at or above this counts as rough or soft ground (boulders, talus, megaripples, loose sand).

hazard_caution_share.source: CAUTION if more than this share of the walked distance crosses rough or soft ground. A few short crossings are normal on Mars; long stretches slow the crew and raise fall risk.

hazard_high.source: CAUTION if any point of the route reaches this hazard level (clearly difficult ground), however short.

hazard_block.source: Cells with terrain hazard at or above this are treated as impassable.

soft_ti_max.source: Thermal inertia below this suggests fine, loose material (soft-ground risk). Jezero TI p5/p50/p95 = 170/234/315 on our grid (Edwards & Buz 2021).

gcr_msv_per_day.source: Curiosity RAD surface dose equivalent rate, ~0.64 mSv/day (Hassler et al. 2014, Science 343).

effort_cases._about: Walking cost = k x Minetti et al. (2002) cost of walking C(i) [J/kg/m] x mass x distance. Minetti is Earth, unsuited treadmill data; k turns it into a range for a suited astronaut on Mars.

low.source: Unsuited, reduced gravity: Farley & McMahon (1992, J Appl Physiol 73:2709) measured ~33% lower walking cost at 25% g; we interpolate ~27% lower at Mars 0.38 g. Faster pace (assumed +20%).

central.source: Suited partial-gravity walking ~ Earth shirtsleeve cost: Earth Shirtsleeve Performance Index 1.0/0.8/0.6 at 10/20/30% grade, lunar gravity, Mark III suit (Norcross et al. 2010, NASA IST-2 report, NTRS 20110003409).

high.source: Pessimistic: full suit+load mass at Earth-equivalent cost, slower pace (assumed -25%). Mars-gravity suited walking data were not found; EVA Walkback Test (NASA/TP-2009-214796) was lunar gravity only.
